correctness.rationale: For p>1 and a,b>=1, weighted AM-GM shows w=lambda z1^a z2^b maps open ellipsoid inside unit disk and w=1 on boundary occurs on gcd(a,b) phase circles. The full, possibly disconnected, kernel H of the torus character (a,b) acts unitarily; Haar averaging a total-degree<=L multiplier removes every monomial except nonnegative integer multiples of (a,b), so unrestricted Q reduces to P(w) with degree <=floor(L/(a+b)). A residual polynomial e(w) of degree N+1 has e(1)=1; orthogonality gives diagonal weights M_n and weighted Cauchy-Schwarz exactly achieves inverse S_(N+1), including explicit optimizer. Stirling establishes M_n~sqrt(2*pi*p*a*b)*(a+b)^(beta-3/2)*n^(beta-1/2), proven for all fixed parameters, giving beta<=3/2 cyclicity and three error regimes. Bounded coordinate multipliers transfer approximation of 1 to cyclicity. On boundary, every probability measure has forced (an,bn) moments lambda^-n; Haar over full H suppresses others and attains exact energy S_infty, hence kernel capacity 1/S_infty. Independent numeric asymptotic checks at four parameter tuples supplement analytic proof; exact kernel normalization and disconnected H are essential.
